title: Powerhouse publishes official Docker images for Connect (frontend + Nginx) and Switchboard (backend API) to ghcr.io
content:
Three official images on `ghcr.io/powerhouse-inc/powerhouse/`: connect (Alpine + Node + Nginx with Brotli), switchboard (Node 24 + Prisma), academy (docs). Tags: latest, dev, staging, vX.Y.Z. Docker Compose stack: connect + switchboard + postgres:16.1. Connect startup: load packages from `PH_REGISTRY_PACKAGES`, `ph connect build`, configure/start Nginx. Switchboard startup: install packages from `PH_PACKAGES`, run Prisma migrations (only if `PH_REACTOR_DATABASE_URL` is set), start the server. Custom packages use a different env var per service: Connect reads `PH_REGISTRY_PACKAGES` (comma-separated, written to a registry config at startup), Switchboard reads `PH_PACKAGES` (comma-separated). Production: use specific version tags, persist postgres with volumes, bind to 127.0.0.1 behind a reverse proxy for SSL termination. `DATABASE_URL` is Switchboard-only -- Connect never uses it -- and it accepts a PostgreSQL *or* SQLite connection string (default `"dev.db"`).

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._

## Superseded at v6.2.2-dev.74
This note describes the pre-redesign Docker layout and is retired. What changed: images are published to the **Vetra Harbor registry** `cr.vetra.io/powerhouse-inc-powerhouse/*` (the `ghcr.io` copies are frozen at the old builds), the tag set gained `rc`, the Connect image is **nginx serving a SPA built at image-build time** with no Node or `ph` CLI (so `PH_REGISTRY_PACKAGES` is not how Connect loads packages any more — the browser loads them from `packageRegistryUrl`), the Switchboard image installs `@powerhousedao/switchboard` from npm and runs **Kysely** rather than Prisma migrations, and `DATABASE_URL` no longer means "PostgreSQL or SQLite, default dev.db" — storage is `PH_REACTOR_DATABASE_URL` / `PH_SWITCHBOARD_DATABASE_URL` with an embedded-PGlite fallback. See the four notes that supersede it.
description: Connect image builds the frontend and serves via Nginx; Switchboard optionally runs Prisma migrations, then starts the API server.
